name: Pan-Germanism
summary: Pan-Germanism seeks to unite all ethnic Germans, or German speakers, and in some versions all Germanic peoples, in one state, and supports German minorities abroad. From the 1890s it became explicitly racial, antisemitic and anti-Slav, and its leading organisation backed imperial expansion, colonies, annexationist war aims and eastward settlement. It opposed democratisation and socialism, and its ideas fed into later Nazi policy of Lebensraum and Heim ins Reich.
scope: The Pan-German movement as Britannica and the scholarship on the League describe it: the drive to unite all German speakers (in some versions all Germanic peoples) in one Greater Germany, carried by the Pan-German League (Alldeutscher Verband, founded 1891, renamed 1894; Hasse, then Claß from 1908) and by Schönerer and Wolf in Austria-Hungary, with its racial, antisemitic, anti-Slav and expansionist turn from the 1890s. Runs from the German nationalism of Jahn and Arndt and the Grossdeutsch solution through the League's wartime and Weimar activity. Excludes the Nazi regime's own policy, except where the sources present the movement as its precursor.

notes: Answers come only from positions the sources state: Britannica on Pan-Germanism, the League and Hasse, Hofmeister's scholarly article, the 1903 League statutes and Claß's programme 'If I Were Kaiser' (Claß chaired the League from 1908). Everything else is null. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, means; the economy, religion, ecology and technology are silent in these sources. The earlier pass's answers came from Wikipedia summaries; those not supported by the cited sources are nulled with their history kept. The Reich League and Schönerer's Austrian strand are not separated in the answers, which follow Claß and Hofmeister.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Claß treats the army and navy as essential, even attack weapons, and Hofmeister reports the League promoting a military dictatorship under Hindenburg and Ludendorff.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Claß says Alsace-Lorraine was taken for military necessity and 'the inhabitants were an extra; the territory was the main thing', and Hofmeister reports plans to annex the Baltic provinces and French land.

arms-reduction.rationale: Claß rejects the view that Germany is 'saturated' and calls the army and navy attack weapons, opposing keeping arms to a bare minimum.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Claß demands that 'decadent' art be banned and that censorship be given to the most recognised masters, to protect the nation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hofmeister describes the League's class-based Volksgemeinschaft and its enforcing of the Burgfrieden, and Claß wants the best from all walks of life to work for reconciliation.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Hofmeister notes the League's concern for the 20 million ethnic Germans living in other states and its 1914 war aims of acquiring land and unifying ethnic Germans in Central Europe.

defeat-communism.rationale: Claß demands suppression of the socialist press, expulsion of socialist leaders and anarchists, and Hofmeister reports Claß's call for suppressing social democracy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Claß rejects a workers' party that has disowned its nation and fatherland, and Hofmeister reports the League enforced the Burgfrieden in 1914.

democracy-best.rationale: Claß calls democracy 'un-German', would replace universal and equal suffrage with a class or plural franchise, and Hofmeister reports the League opposed democratisation.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Claß calls for generous state funding to bring ethnic Germans back from Russia, Galicia and North America and to settle them within the Empire.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Claß rules women out of politics and assigns them the instinctive task of raising children to love the fatherland.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Hofmeister says the League treated the ethnic complexity of German society as a problem to be solved by ethnic homogenisation and enforced cultural homogenisation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Claß says political rights should be regulated by the service each person renders the totality and by behaviour toward it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Claß would bar Jews from owning German newspapers, directing banks or owning rural land, and expropriate Polish land.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Claß would hold strikers in protective custody without appeal and change laws on personal freedom that stand in the way, and Hofmeister reports League propaganda for a military dictatorship in 1917-18.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Claß says the axiom 'equal rights for all' must be replaced by rights regulated by service to the whole, and places resident Jews under an Aliens' Law barring them from office, the vote and professions.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The League's 1903 statutes hold that all parts of the German people belong together racially and culturally, and Hofmeister describes its aim of an ethnically and politically homogeneous German Empire.

harm-principle.rationale: Claß would ban decadent art, restrict the press and put 'un-German' associations under prohibition, restricting adults well beyond preventing harm to others.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: Claß defends an aggressive policy and pre-emptive strikes ('defensive' wars conducted aggressively) and Hofmeister reports annexationist war aims.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Britannica defines Pan-Germanism as the aim of political unification of all German speakers, and for some adherents all Germanic-language peoples, including Dutch, Flemish and Scandinavians.

majority-settlement.rationale: Claß would give the state powers of expropriation of Polish and Danish land to settle Germans, and Hofmeister reports plans to settle Germans in annexed Baltic land.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Claß says the army and navy are also attack weapons and expansion in Europe comes through victorious wars, and Hofmeister's 1914 war aims included annexations in France, the Baltic and Poland.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hofmeister reports that in 1917-18 the League blamed Jews for undermining wartime unity, and Claß spread early stab-in-the-back claims and spoke of 'Pan-Judaism'.

minority-language-support.rationale: Claß demands Polish papers carry German translation, bans French and Danish from schools, courts and churches, and would end Danish administration, the opposite of supporting minority languages.

nation-first.rationale: The statutes commit the League to an active policy of pursuing German interests throughout the world, and Claß calls for an aggressive foreign policy.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Claß would abolish private schools in Alsace-Lorraine, rule it dictatorially and force Danes to declare for Prussia or leave; Hofmeister adds enforced cultural homogenisation as a League aim.

national-rebirth.rationale: Claß presents reform of the Empire as essential to stave off catastrophe, wants a 'return to health' in culture, morals and politics, and the seed of degeneration killed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Claß has the state publish cheap newspapers, regulate the press, require general-education examinations, censor art and settle Germans in the east.

open-borders.rationale: Claß demands the borders be totally and unconditionally barred to Jewish immigration and all non-German aliens expelled and kept out.

patriotic-education.rationale: Claß makes German history obligatory and wants soldiers and schools to teach national themes, and the League's statutes aim to shape schooling in keeping with German ethnicity.

population-transfer.rationale: Claß's programme expels foreign Jews, non-German aliens, socialist leaders and French or Danish residents who refuse loyalty, and Hofmeister reports Claß and Gebsattel demanded expelling peoples from their homelands.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Claß makes Danes and French residents who will not declare for the German state cross the border, and Hofmeister reports ethnic Germans were to be settled eastward.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The 1903 statutes commit the League to preserving German ethnicity in Europe and overseas and supporting it in threatened areas.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Claß would bar the borders totally and unconditionally to Jewish immigration, defined by descent, and sort other foreigners by race-relatedness.

race-social-construct.rationale: The League's statutes rest on Germans belonging together racially, and Hofmeister reports it radicalised racism and Social Darwinism.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: Claß accepts that victorious wars bring cessions of territory and Hofmeister reports the League's war aims of annexing land after victory.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Claß demands that all non-German aliens be expelled as swiftly as possible and then kept out, and that Jewish immigration be barred entirely.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Claß wants all non-German aliens expelled from the Empire and Hofmeister says Claß demanded suppression of Jews and Slavs and resettlement of Eastern European Jews outside German-held lands.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Claß would let employers place a factory area under strike protection, ban gatherings and strike posts, and detain violators summarily without appeal.

sacred-nation.rationale: Claß writes that the nation is eternal, takes precedence over individual personalities, and that its perpetuity is the highest principle of life.

single-official-language.rationale: Claß would make German the only tolerated language in assemblies, schools and courts in Alsace-Lorraine and for Poles, and abolish Danish in schools, churches and administration.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Claß calls for aggressive foreign policy and has the army support national indoctrination, and the League's wartime aims required Germany's victory.

state-harmful.rationale: Pan-Germanism aims to unite Germans in one nation-state per Britannica, and Claß demands a state that defends itself against its enemies.

strong-leader.rationale: Claß's 'If I Were Kaiser' says the best of the people long for a strong and virtuous leader and hopes the crown bearer will be one, since greatness comes only through subordination to a leader.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Hofmeister reports Claß demanded political suppression of social democracy, left-liberalism and the Centre Party as 'enemies of the empire', and Claß's text would ban socialist assemblies and press.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hasse's Deutsche Politik declares 'We want territory, even if it be inhabited by foreign peoples', and Claß writes that Germany will have to acquire territory.

women-suffrage.rationale: Claß states that the political strivings of women cannot be regarded as justifiable or useful and ties this to his discussion of voting rights.

workers-nation.rationale: Claß would expel the leaders of socialist parties and unions because they disowned the fatherland, and win the masses back to the nation through national holidays and press.
